R3.1.focus: Identify the role of a proton acceptor.

questions.prompt: In H₂O + H⁺ → H₃O⁺, H₂O accepts a proton. Is it acting as an acid or a base?
questions.hint: A Brønsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.
questions.working: H₂O is acting as a base because it accepts H⁺.

questions.prompt: In NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺, NH₃ accepts a proton. Is it acting as an acid or a base?
questions.hint: A Brønsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.

questions.prompt: In OH⁻ + H⁺ → H₂O, OH⁻ accepts a proton. Is it acting as an acid or a base?
questions.hint: A Brønsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.

questions.prompt: In F⁻ + H⁺ → HF, F⁻ accepts a proton. Is it acting as an acid or a base?
questions.hint: A Brønsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.

questions.prompt: In HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ → H₂CO₃, HCO₃⁻ accepts a proton. Is it acting as an acid or a base?
questions.hint: A Brønsted–Lowry base accepts a proton.
questions.working: HCO₃⁻ is acting as a base by accepting a proton.
